Read fixed-width ASCII file using SPSS or SAS Setup file

Source: R/read_ascii_setup.R
read_ascii_setup.Rd

read_ascii_setup() is used when you need to read a fixed-width ASCII (text) file that comes with a setup file. The setup file provides instructions on how to create and name the columns, and fix the key-value pairs (sometimes called value labels). This is common in government data, particularly data produced before 2010.

Usage

read_ascii_setup(
  data,
  setup_file,
  use_value_labels = TRUE,
  use_clean_names = TRUE,
  select_columns = NULL,
  coerce_numeric = TRUE,
  missing_values = c("all", "active", "none")
)

Arguments

data

Name of the ASCII (.txt or .dat) file that contains the data. This file may be zipped with a file extension of .zip.

setup_file

Name of the SPSS or SAS setup file - should be a .sps or .sas (.txt also accepted as are these files in zipped format). See parse_setup for how the type is determined.

use_value_labels

If TRUE, fixes value labels of the data. e.g. If a column is "sex" and has values of 0 or 1, and the setup file says 0 = male and 1 = female, it will make that change.

use_clean_names

If TRUE fixes column names from default column name in the setup file (e.g. V1, V2) to the descriptive label for the column provided in the file (e.g. age, sex, etc.).

select_columns

Specify which columns from the dataset you want. If NULL, will return all columns. Accepts the column number (e.g. 1:5), column name (e.g. V1, V2, etc.) or column label (e.g. VICTIM_NAME, CITY, etc.).

coerce_numeric

If TRUE (default) will make columns where all values can be made numeric into numeric columns. Every value is checked, so a column with any text value stays character. Columns the setup file says are text (SPSS "(A)", SAS "$") always stay character, so their leading zeros are kept. Useful as FALSE if other variables have leading zeros - such as US Census FIPS codes given as numbers.

Columns that the setup file gives implied decimal places (e.g. V7 37-43 (1) in SPSS or V7 37-43 .1 in SAS) get their decimal point whatever coerce_numeric is: a value of "0000785" with 1 implied decimal place becomes 78.5, or the text "000078.5" if coerce_numeric is FALSE. Values that already have a decimal point are kept as they are.

missing_values

Which of the setup file's missing values to set to NA. Setup files often have their missing values section commented out (e.g. "* MISSING VALUES" in SPSS or inside /* */ in SAS) so that the codes stay in the data unless the user chooses otherwise.

"all"

(default) Use every missing value in the setup file, ignoring whether it is commented out. This is what earlier versions did.

"active"

Use only the missing values that aren't commented out, as SPSS and SAS would.

"none"

Don't use any missing values; every code is kept.

Missing values are matched by value, as in SPSS and SAS, so a missing value written 9 also matches 09 or 0000009 in the data, except in columns the setup file says are text (SPSS "(A)", SAS "$"), where it must be the same text. Value labels are applied first, so a missing value that also has a value label (e.g. 9 = "Unknown") keeps its label rather than becoming NA unless use_value_labels = FALSE.

Value

data.frame of the data from the ASCII file

Value labels

As in SPSS and SAS, codes of number columns are matched by value (a label for 0 labels 0000000), and codes of text columns (SPSS "(A)", SAS "$") must be the same text; a blank or the letters NA in a text column can have a label. As in SPSS, a VALUE LABELS command replaces any labels an earlier VALUE LABELS command gave a column, and ADD VALUE LABELS adds to them (changing the label of a code that already has one).

Recodes

Only a setup file's layout, names, value labels and missing values are used. Statements that change values (SAS IF v = 1 THEN v = 5;, SPSS RECODE v (1=5)) aren't applied, and a message lists them.

Blank values

A blank, a lone "." or the letters NA in a number column is NA. A blank or the letters NA in a text column is NA unless it has a value label (and use_value_labels is TRUE), which is used instead.

Messages

read_ascii_setup() tells you with a message when it:

  • adds implied decimal places to a column's values (listing the columns and their decimal places),

  • finds values in such a column that equal one of its codes (value labels or missing values) only before the decimal places are applied, which suggests the data doesn't match the setup file,

  • finds SAS value labels for ranges of values or OTHER, which aren't applied (only when use_value_labels = TRUE),

  • sets values to NA because of missing values that are commented out in the setup file (only when missing_values = "all"),

  • makes column names unique because two columns would have had the same name (only when use_clean_names = TRUE),

  • uses only the last of several different sets of value labels a column has (only when use_value_labels = TRUE),

  • skips SAS missing value statements it can't read (only when missing_values isn't "none"),

  • finds statements that change values (recodes), which aren't applied,

  • selects, by select_columns, the first of several columns that had the same name (saying what the others are called now), or

  • reads a setup file that isn't valid UTF-8 as Windows-1252.

suppressMessages(read_ascii_setup(...)) silences them. They have the class "asciiSetupReader_message", so suppressMessages(read_ascii_setup(...), classes = "asciiSetupReader_message") silences only these messages. Each kind also has its own class: "asciiSetupReader_implied_decimals", "asciiSetupReader_unscaled_codes", "asciiSetupReader_label_ranges", "asciiSetupReader_commented_missing", "asciiSetupReader_unique_names", "asciiSetupReader_replaced_labels", "asciiSetupReader_skipped_missing", "asciiSetupReader_recodes", "asciiSetupReader_select_columns" and "asciiSetupReader_encoding".

Errors

Setup files that can't be read stop with an error of class "asciiSetupReader_error" and a more specific class: "asciiSetupReader_delimited" (a file for delimited, not fixed-width, data), "asciiSetupReader_no_positions" (no column positions, e.g. a file of value labels only) or "asciiSetupReader_unsupported_input" (an SPSS DATA LIST or SAS INPUT statement this package can't read, e.g. one with several records per case). A select_columns that names or numbers columns the setup file doesn't have stops with an error of class "asciiSetupReader_select_columns".

Examples

# Text file is zipped to save space.
dataset_name <- system.file("extdata", "example_data.zip",
  package = "asciiSetupReader")
sps_name <- system.file("extdata", "example_setup.sps",
  package = "asciiSetupReader")

example <- read_ascii_setup(data = dataset_name,
  setup_file = sps_name)

# Does not fix value labels
example2 <- read_ascii_setup(data = dataset_name,
  setup_file = sps_name, use_value_labels = FALSE)

# Keeps original column names
example3 <- read_ascii_setup(data = dataset_name,
  setup_file = sps_name, use_clean_names = FALSE)

# Only returns the first 5 columns
example4 <- read_ascii_setup(data = dataset_name,
  setup_file = sps_name, select_columns = 1:5)

# Only uses the missing values that aren't commented out
example5 <- read_ascii_setup(data = dataset_name,
  setup_file = sps_name, missing_values = "active")
